Julian Assange: Despite Congressional Standoff, NSA Has Secret Authority to Continue Spying Unabated

The sunset clause is June the 1st, and so Ron Wyden and Rand Paul engaged in a filibuster, pushing the passage of the renewal of the PATRIOT Act off to a week where Congress had scheduled to be away all the way leading up to June 1st. So unless there’s an emergency recall of enough of the Senate and Congress, the sunset clause will hit, and that means there will have to be a new PATRIOT Act reintroduced. So it will have to be resuscitated as opposed to having a rollover, and that’s a more involved process. However, our sources say that the NSA is not too concerned, that it has secret interpretations of other authorities that give it much the same power that it would have had under the secret interpretation of 215 and other areas of the USA PATRIOT Act.

Did anyone really think it would be so easy to shut this program down??
Steps in the right direction have to start somewhere, but it will be a long, hard trek if we are going to scale back our surveillance state.
I agree, better this than not trying. But we can't sound the trumpets just yet, lots more work to do, like this new Freedom Act.

We have finally killed the monster that started it all at least. It will be much, much more difficult to enact a new "PATRIOT" Act from scratch, and this is the first step towards rolling back the NSA's authority. There may well be other laws or secret orders that give them the ability to continue and one by one they will be revealed to the public and shut down!

It looks like they are just going to re-name it (USA Freedom Act) and continue on:

So the alternative proposal, which is something that was in the USA FREEDOM Act, which is pretty misnamed—it is a sort of milder version of the USA PATRIOT Act, in some ways. Instead, Verizon and the other—AT&T and other big telcos will hold the information, ready for the National Security Agency. But, you know, it doesn’t make much of a difference if that’s an automated system. It’s just—you know, 80 percent of the National Security Agency is outsourced anyway, in terms of the management of its data. In this case, if it has automatic connections to AT&T and Verizon, there’s no difference in terms of its searching ability. Now, in terms of whether there’s warrants that are used for searches, it is perhaps an aid, because the companies could be made legally liable—that’s up to Congress—for not insisting on a warrant to access that information. I rather suspect that Congress won’t mandate that the companies can’t hand over information unless there’s a warrant.

Now, it’s interesting to contrast that with the situation here in Europe. So, in Europe, there was legislation that telcos should hold that information for 18 months. Now, in Germany, that has been found—in fact, at the European Court level, has been found to be unconstitutional. And in Germany, it was ordered that all that information be flushed away. And now there’s a fight on with various European states, such as Sweden, insisting that they can retain the information, even though the laws of Europe say that they’re not permitted to retain that information.

Pollogo.com is a site that allows people such as twitch streamers to poll their audience, allowing much more audience participation. What do you guys think could be improved? I know there's no shiny results graph yet, but that is the next feature planned as of right now.

Features:

  • Image polls (you can upload images as poll options)
  • Poll closing (polls can be closed after a certain amount of time)
  • Simple, easy to use interface.
  • View count
Hey /v/gaming, a friend of mine created Pollogo.com. Opinions?

Seems pretty cool. I just went over and tested it out, and the poll creation process was smooth and easy. I like that you can pick when it times out, and that the poll actually displays when it's going to be timed out. I know that on twitch, strawpolls just kind of.. pop up in the chat window for me. I don't know whether that's a feature of twitch or a feature of the BetterTTV extension, but man it would be convenient if you could get somebody to adopt that.

The only suggestions I could think of are this:

  • The graph idea is good, I'd definitely go with adding that.

-Maybe you/your friend would add an option to archive polls? This is one thing I could think of that would maybe separate you from the competition.

I think of it this way: Users can create accounts, and users with accounts, if they wish, can archive their poll to their profile so it can be seen later on, or save a copy of the results of their poll locally. As it applies to twitch, I see that being great in a situation where chat is deciding things for a streamer, you can see exactly how chat voted, etc.
